findings.drop_reason: Proven not to be a regression: the guard is required, and the only other affected module (NaruServe-kotlin) has identical output.
findings.title: javadoc onlyIf guard: needed for the proxy and changes no other module's output
findings.description: The guard skips javadoc when a module's main Java sources are only package-info.java. Running javadoc on the proxy package-info alone reproduces 'error: No public or protected classes found to document', so the guard is needed. The only other module it touches is NaruServe-kotlin, which has no Java sources. Its javadoc task goes from NO-SOURCE to SKIPPED, and its javadoc jar stays manifest-only as before. Every other module still runs javadoc (UP-TO-DATE).

findings.drop_reason: The AC only requires the file to exist, and the published NaruServe-kotlin jar is already the same. No failure could be shown.
findings.title: The proxy -javadoc.jar is staged but holds only a manifest
findings.description: FR-REL-006 AC-3 requires a -javadoc.jar, and checkCentralStaging only checks that the file exists. The staged naruserve-proxy-0.11.0-javadoc.jar holds only META-INF/MANIFEST.MF. The already-published naruserve-kotlin javadoc jar is the same, and Maven Central requires only that the jar is present.

findings.drop_reason: This is redundant code, not a test that cannot fail; the exact-set assertion already gives the coverage. It is listed under clean_code CC-001.
findings.title: Banned-prefix loops after an exact-set assertEquals can never fail
findings.description: con_BUILD_019_AC4 (and ReleaseScriptTextTest.fr_REL_006_AC5, lines 190-199) first asserts that runtime == {NaruServe-api}, then loops over runtime looking for banned prefixes. Once the first assertion passes, the loop cannot fail. Each test as a whole can still fail.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the loops, or replace the exact-set assertion with the banned-prefix check.

findings.title: The staging probe runs checkCentralStaging's actions from another task
findings.description: STAGING_PROBE calls check.actions.each { it.execute(check) } so it can run the verify action without the clean and publish steps. This relies on Gradle task-action internals and could break on a Gradle upgrade. On the pinned 8.14.3 it passes deterministically.

The comment-stripping of the extraCompileOnly block repeats the stripping inside mainDependencyEntries (697-707). A shared 'code of a def X = [ ... ] block' helper would cover both.
